Animal travel works best when the desk keeps the process calm, clear, and humane.

Companion Animal Travel Desk
Purpose: This section sets the standard for checking in pets and coordinating safe, courteous travel support for Aurelia Skyways.

Staff must greet every traveler with a steady tone, confirm the animal is fit for carriage, and explain the next steps in plain language. The welcome team should prepare the passenger for boarding, watch for signs of stress, and keep handling gentle at all times. When a crate is required, staff must inspect it for sound construction, secure latches, and enough interior space for the animal to stand, turn, and settle without crowding. <<FACT F071>> Any crate that fails the check must be refused until it meets the rule. Staff should also verify labels, documents, and contact details before the animal moves to the secure area.

For bird travel, the desk must confirm the crate and pet together meet the approved limit before acceptance. <<FACT F065>> If the combined load is too high, staff must advise the traveler to repack or make other arrangements. Use calm, direct wording and never rush the customer through the correction. If a traveler arrives uncertain, the agent should give brief guidance, point out the needed changes, and keep the discussion focused on safety and comfort.

Animals are never to be left unattended in public areas, and any sign of illness, escape risk, or unsafe crate condition must be escalated at once. The handler should choose humane methods, avoid sudden movements, and keep noise low near boarding lanes. If a special case comes up, the desk should pause the process and seek a supervisor review before proceeding.

Contact the senior coordinator or the duty supervisor if any case falls outside this guidance.
